description:
THE LAW (fz-kdt.129 refutation, 2026-09-01 -- which BLOCKED the first
129 build with a 5-line reproducer): an arm's RuntimeTypePredicate is
COARSER than the surface it was projected from (list shape erases
elements; tuple arity erases payloads), so a value can satisfy every
question an arm asks and still lie outside the surface that arm's body
was compiled for. Seating that arm first routes the value into a body
whose representation never named it. Reproducer (base green all doors
both schedules; the blocked commit aborted JIT+AOT both schedules):

  dbg(Enum.all?([:ok, :ok])); dbg(Enum.empty?([:ok, :ok]));
  dbg(Enum.all?([1, 2]))

-- the list(int) x {all?/1} arm seated ahead of its
list(:ok) x {all?/1, empty?} sibling because its callable SET is
strictly smaller; [:ok,:ok] carrying all?/1 satisfies BOTH its
questions and reaches the int-list body ->
fz_list_head_int_ref abort. Interp's dynamic tags hide it; the corpus
stdout sweep passes (the THIRD time a whole-corpus sweep shipped a
dispatch defect -- lib-level adversarial gates are the only gate for
this class).

BOTH prior orderings fail this law in opposite directions:
surface-narrowest-first (129's ticket candidate) and
test-narrowest-first (129's first build). THE SOUND CONDITION: an arm
may be seated before another only when, per position, its test
SEPARATES them there OR its own surface CONTAINS the later arm's
(surface coverage). Where no seat is covering-safe for a pair, the
pair is the fz-kdt.107 inseparable class ONE RUNG WIDER than
arms-asking-one-question, and no ordering rule may pretend otherwise.

Measured corpus scope: 2 blind-escape seats at the blocked head vs 1
at base, both in enum_predicate_search, benign there only by a
correlation the compiler never proved (Enum.empty?'s reducer never
carries {:cont,...}). The pre-existing base escape is a standing
latent hazard of arrival order too -- record it, don't pretend base
is clean.

ALSO OWNED HERE (the original 131 finding, the third facet):
distinguishable arms whose tests OVERLAP without containment
({A,B} vs {B,C}) -- seating decides which body runs for the overlap =
meaning. Cure upstream for all facets: tests that do not overlap
unless surfaces do (fz-kdt.119 exact tuple tags; fz-kdt.107 step 3
list elements); re-census the blind-escape and overlap populations
after those land. Sequence after fz-kdt.119.

comments.text: fz-kdt.119 review correction (2026-09-01): overlaps_on_an_erasing_axis's doc calls ints/floats exact ('a value passes only by being in the tested set, which the arm's surface names') -- but runtime_type_predicate stores ints/floats as PRESENCE BITS only and ignores descr.brands unless cofinite, so two arms with surfaces 'brand X of int' / 'brand Y of int' have EQUAL tests and incomparable surfaces, and covers declares the position non-erasing and seats freely. Benign today (brands are runtime-erased by design, reprs identical -- fz-bsx) but the doc claim is false as written and becomes a live hole if numeric singletons return (the predicate's own comment says they are recoverable from history). Correct the doc claim when this ticket or 119 next touches the file. ALSO: 119 partially unblocks this ticket (tuple pairs gain separation and leave the neither-covers population; LIST pairs do not -- the queue does not empty).

title: A seat must carry surface coverage: any arm ordering not covering-safe is unsound wherever the test is blind to what the body relies on
